title: Exercise After Having a Baby in NZ – Safe Return to the Gym
meta_desc: Learn postpartum recovery timelines, pelvic floor care, and NZ gyms with crèche. Practical steps to get back to exercise safely.
intro: Having a baby is a massive physical event, and getting back to the gym can feel daunting. This guide walks you through the typical recovery timeline, key pelvic‑floor work, and which New Zealand gyms make post‑natal training easier with on‑site crèches and supportive programmes.

sections.heading: Post‑natal Recovery Timeline
sections.body: Most health professionals advise a gradual return to moderate activity after the first six weeks, provided you’ve had a normal vaginal birth and no complications. The first two weeks are best spent on gentle walking and breathing exercises to promote circulation and reduce swelling. By weeks 3‑6 you can introduce low‑impact cardio and basic pelvic‑floor activation. Full‑strength training usually becomes safe around weeks 8‑12, but listen to your body and get clearance from your GP or midwife.
list: Weeks 0‑2: Light walking, diaphragmatic breathing, ankle pumps
Weeks 3‑6: Low‑impact cardio (e.g., stationary bike), basic pelvic‑floor contractions
Weeks 7‑12: Light resistance work, gradual increase in load
After 12 weeks: Full strength training if pain‑free and cleared

sections.heading: Pelvic Floor and Core Rehab
sections.body: A strong pelvic floor reduces the risk of urinary incontinence—a condition that affects about 30 % of postpartum women in New Zealand, according to the Ministry of Health. Start with slow, isolated contractions (Kegels) and progress to functional movements that engage the deep core (e.g., dead‑bugs, bird‑dogs). Research shows that a 6‑week programme of targeted pelvic‑floor exercises can improve muscle strength by up to 40 %.
list: Do 3 sets of 10‑15 slow Kegels, holding each contraction for 5‑8 seconds
Add core‑stability drills like dead‑bugs once you can hold a plank for 20 seconds
Avoid heavy abdominal crunches until you can comfortably engage the transverse abdominis

sections.heading: Gyms with Crèche and Post‑natal Support
sections.body: Choosing a gym that offers on‑site child care removes a major barrier for new mums. In NZ, the YMCA network, Les Mills gyms, and Contours all provide crèches and specific post‑natal classes. Many of these clubs also participate in the Exercise NZ subsidised scheme, giving eligible families 40‑70 % off the standard membership price.
list: All three clubs run post‑natal HIIT and low‑impact classes designed by certified physiotherapists
Exercise NZ members can claim up to 70 % off, reducing the cost to as low as $24 / mo

sections.heading: Gentle Return Programme – 4‑Week Sample
sections.body: The following plan assumes you’ve cleared your GP for moderate activity. Each week includes a mix of cardio, strength, and pelvic‑floor work, with optional crèche hours noted for convenience.
list: Week 1 – 3 × 30‑min walks, 2 × 10‑min pelvic‑floor routine, 1 × 30‑min low‑impact class (e.g., Contours Gentle Flow) – use crèche for 1‑hour sessions
Week 2 – Add 2 × 20‑min stationary bike, continue pelvic‑floor work, introduce 1 × 15‑min bodyweight circuit (squats, lunges) – crèche for 1‑hour
Week 3 – Increase bike to 30 min, add 2 × 10‑min core stability (dead‑bugs, bird‑dogs), keep pelvic‑floor daily – crèche for 1‑hour
Week 4 – 2 × 30‑min cardio (bike or treadmill), 2 × 15‑min resistance (machines, light dumbbells), daily pelvic‑floor – crèche for 1‑hour

sections.heading: Take the Next Step
sections.body: Feeling ready to re‑join a gym? Use our free comparison tool to see which NZ clubs match your budget, location, and crèche needs, and check if you qualify for the Exercise NZ subsidy. A stronger, healthier you starts with the right support.
